📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before you buy household goods, clothes, or toys, look for a free store or swap shop near you, where people leave usable things for others to take at no cost. Try your town’s transfer station or recycling center, the library’s events calendar, and local churches. Bring only clean, working items, and take only what you’ll use.

Despite the name, many swap shops don’t require a swap. A family short on money or settling into an empty apartment can leave with a lamp, a set of dishes, or a bag of toys without bringing a thing.

Most sit at the town’s transfer station or recycling drop-off, where residents who haul their own trash leave household goods that still work, from kitchenware and tools to books and small furniture. Many are open only to residents, and some check for a transfer station sticker.

It has been revealed that free stores work the same way, away from the transfer station. Churches and nonprofits run them, mostly for clothing and household basics, and some limit how much you take per visit. Public libraries hold swap days. Pop-up free markets, some called Really Really Free Markets, run once a month, often in a park. A toy swap or a book swap sticks to one kind of thing.

Industry observers note that call 211 or search 211.org for free stores near you, and check the library’s events calendar for swap days. If you’ve just moved, get your transfer station sticker before your first visit. Bring what your household has outgrown, too. Parents who drop off kids’ clothes at a swap may leave with the next size up.

Then follow the posted rules, which usually include these:.

Sources indicate that if your town has no swap shop, ask its public works department or recycling committee to add one at the transfer station. Massachusetts’ environmental agency even offers towns grants for one. Until then, host a clothing swap with friends, and ask your Buy Nothing group for the specific things you need.

Search your town’s website for “swap shop” or “swap shed” before your next shopping trip, since the swap shop’s page lists the hours, the rules, and whether you need a sticker.

  • Paying cash for new equipment can leave your business short for payroll and inventory.
  • Buying outright looks thrifty, and it usually costs less over an asset’s life than leasing, the U.S.
  • Industry observers note that so each option comes down to two numbers, the cash it takes up front and its total cost over the years you’ll use it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paying cash for new equipment can leave your business short for payroll and inventory. Before you buy, get quotes on a lease, a used model with a dealer warranty, and a repair of what you have. Then compare each one’s total cost over the years you’ll use it, after taxes.

Buying outright looks thrifty, and it usually costs less over an asset’s life than leasing, the U.S. Small Business Administration notes. But that saving builds over years, while the whole price leaves your account the day you buy.

Industry observers note that so each option comes down to two numbers, the cash it takes up front and its total cost over the years you’ll use it. With latest equipment, lowering one raises the other. A lease takes little cash up front but usually costs more in total than paying cash, and so does an equipment loan, once you add interest and fees. Buying the same model used lowers both, as long as it has plenty of working years left.

It has been revealed that at tax time, lease payments are deductible as rent, while Section 179 of the tax code lets you deduct a purchase’s full price the year you start using it, up to yearly limits. A lease you can buy out for a token sum, such as $1, generally counts as a purchase to the IRS, so have a tax pro run each option’s after-tax cost.

Lease what you’d trade for a newer model within a few years, like computers. Before you sign, check how the lease ends: the buyout price, who pays to ship the equipment back, and how much notice stops it from renewing on its own.

It has been revealed that buy used from a dealer that inspects or refurbishes the equipment and puts a warranty in writing. A restaurant that pays $9,000 for a two-year-old, dealer-certified range, when the same model costs $22,000 upcoming, keeps $13,000 as a cushion for its first slow season.

Recent findings suggest that repair what you have when the repair costs less per year of use than a replacement. Say a $1,500 repair keeps an old range going three more years, and a $9,000 used one would last 10 years. The repair costs $500 a year, the replacement $900.

Then pick the lowest total among the options that leave enough cash to cover your slowest month’s payroll, rent, and supplier bills.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you work 900 or more hours a school year as a preschool or K-12 teacher, aide, counselor, or principal, you can deduct up to $350 of classroom costs you paid yourself, even if you take the standard deduction.
  • Sources indicate that every dollar of it comes off the income you’re taxed on, so in the 22% tax bracket, each $100 you deduct cuts your federal tax by $22.
  • The IRS’s list of qualifying costs covers books, supplies, computers and software, other equipment and materials you use in class, and professional development courses related to your subject or your students.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you work 900 or more hours a school year as a preschool or K-12 teacher, aide, counselor, or principal, you can deduct up to $350 of classroom costs you paid yourself, even if you take the standard deduction. Keep the receipts for books, supplies, and training, and claim the deduction on Schedule 1 of your federal return.

Sources indicate that every dollar of it comes off the income you’re taxed on, so in the 22% tax bracket, each $100 you deduct cuts your federal tax by $22. Starting with 2026 expenses, a second deduction can cover what you spend above the cap.

The IRS’s list of qualifying costs covers books, supplies, computers and software, other equipment and materials you use in class, and professional development courses related to your subject or your students. In health and gym classes, supplies count only if they’re athletic. Leave out anything your school, a grant, or another source paid you back for.

A law signed in September 2026 extends the deduction to preschool and child care educators who meet the same 900-hour test, starting with 2026 expenses. Married educators filing jointly can each deduct up to $350.

The second deduction goes on Schedule A, the form where you itemize, or list your deductions instead of taking the standard deduction. The tax code sets no dollar limit on it, extends it to school coaches and athletic administrators, and covers nonathletic supplies for health and gym classes. It pays off only when your itemized deductions, such as mortgage interest and state and local taxes, add up to more than your standard deduction.

A third-grade teacher who itemizes and spends $450 on books and supplies deducts $350 on Schedule 1 and the other $100 on Schedule A.

In a recent development, keep every receipt in one folder, paper or photos, with a note on what each item was for. The IRS generally has three years after you file to charge you more tax, so keep the folder at least that long.

This is what travel rewards done right looks like: not flying business class because you're wealthy, but because you understood the system better than the airlines expected you to.

The core insight here is understanding how Virgin Atlantic prices its own metal versus partner awards — and then deliberately choosing the right one for the right job.

Industry observers note that virgin Atlantic's Flying Club is famous in the points community for two things. First, its partner award sweet spots: ANA First Class for as low as 55,000–60,000 miles one-way, Delta One at competitive rates. These are the headline acts. But quietly sitting in the same award chart is a genuinely underappreciated gem — Virgin's own short-haul European business class, priced at a flat 17,500 miles regardless of the specific route within that distance band.

Industry observers note that why does Virgin price it this way? Virgin Atlantic operates as a premium carrier and sets its award chart to reflect aspirational redemptions — the kind that make Flying Club membership feel worthwhile. For long-haul routes on their own metal, their pricing is competitive but not exceptional. For short-haul Europe, however, the fixed pricing creates an opportunity: a two-hour flight to Rome or Athens costs the same 17,500 miles as a cheaper, shorter hop, but those premium routes have cash prices that routinely spike into the thousands. The chart wasn't built to be a loophole — it's just that cash prices for short-haul business class in Europe are genuinely volatile and often extraordinary.

Industry observers note that the fuel surcharge reality check. Here's where you need to pay close attention. Virgin Atlantic is known for passing fuel surcharges onto award redemptions on their own flights. This is the opposite of what happens on ANA or Delta partner awards booked through Flying Club (which carry zero surcharges). On a short-haul European route, those surcharges are real but typically far more manageable than on a transatlantic segment — often in the $50–$150 range rather than $500+. The CPP math still works strongly in your favor, but you should go in with eyes open: this is not a zero-cash-outlay redemption.

In a recent development, the transfer path is exceptional. This is where the ChooseFI community has a serious structural advantage. Virgin Atlantic Flying Club accepts transfers from essentially every major points currency:.

Every major transferable currency gets you there at a 1:1 ratio with instant speed. That means if you're holding Chase points from your Sapphire Reserve or Preferred, Amex points from your Gold or Platinum, or Citi points from your Premier card, you have a direct, frictionless pipeline to 17,500 Virgin miles within minutes of finding availability. This is critical because, as you'll learn in the booking section, Virgin availability on its own short-haul European routes can be limited, and you want to be able to move fast when a seat opens up.

The booking window opens 331 days in advance — use it. Miles don't expire as long as you have account activity within 36 months, so there's no pressure to burn them before you're ready.

Before you touch a single website, clarify your mission: you're looking for Virgin Atlantic-operated business class availability on short-haul European routes departing from London Heathrow (LHR). This is not a search for partner award space — this is VS metal, VS availability, VS seats. Your most common target routes will be LHR → FCO (Rome), LHR → ATH (Athens), and similar European city pairs. Build your itinerary around where VS actually flies in Europe, not every possible destination.

According to recent reports, go to virginatlantic.com and use the award search tool. Select "Book with miles" and enter your route. Virgin demonstrates its own availability directly here — you don't need a third-party search engine for this specific redemption. Search one-way rather than round-trip so you can see each direction independently. If your target dates show no availability, flex by ±3 days. Business class award seats on short-haul routes are typically released in small batches.

Recent findings suggest that open a second browser tab and search the same route and date on Google Flights or directly on virginatlantic.com for a revenue ticket. Note the cash price for business class. This is your CPP sanity check — if the cash price is $1,200 and you're spending 17,500 miles plus ~$100 in surcharges, you're at roughly 6.3 cents per point. If the cash price is $2,500, your CPP jumps dramatically. This step helps you prioritize which dates to target.

Sources indicate that do NOT transfer points until you have confirmed award availability on your target date. Transfers to Virgin are one-directional and cannot be reversed.

Sources indicate that once you've confirmed a seat is available, transfer your points from your chosen program. For Chase, Amex, Citi, and Bilt transfers, the miles land in your Flying Club account instantly. Refresh your Flying Club account, confirm the miles are there, and complete the booking before the seat disappears. Enter your payment details for the taxes and surcharges (typically $50–$150 on short-haul European routes).

Virgin Atlantic operates its own short-haul flights from London Heathrow to destinations across Europe including Amsterdam, Paris, Edinburgh, Geneva, and Athens. These are different from partner codeshare flights. The 17,500-point price applies specifically to Virgin Atlantic-operated short-haul business class. Partner flights (booked through Flying Club but operated by Delta, KLM, or Air France) use a different award chart and typically cost significantly more. When searching, filter for Virgin Atlantic flight numbers (VS prefix) to find the sweet spot pricing. The business class product on short-haul includes a dedicated cabin, lounge access at Heathrow, priority boarding, and meal service.

Let's walk through a real scenario that illustrates exactly what this redemption looks like in practice.

Sources indicate that the Setup: You've just arrived at London Heathrow on a transatlantic award — perhaps an ANA First Class redemption through the very same Flying Club program. Do this: Use it as a positioning flight on a broader trip This redemption was practically designed for trip architecture. Recent findings suggest that do this: Compare cash prices before transferring Not all dates are created equal. Industry observers note that avoid this: Confusing this with partner award bookings Virgin's zero-surcharge policy applies to partner airlines like ANA and Delta. This redemption is built for a specific type of ChooseFI traveler: the intermediate-to-advanced points strategist who thinks in itineraries, not individual flights.

The ideal candidate is someone who's already planning a trip that routes through London Heathrow — perhaps on a transatlantic award — and needs an elegant, high-value way to reach their final European destination. Solo travelers and couples benefit most here. At 17,500 miles per person, a couple needs 35,000 Virgin miles, which is completely achievable with a single transfer from a combined Chase or Amex balance.

Sources indicate that families should approach with caution. This redemption scores a 2/5 for family-friendliness for good reason. Multiplying 17,500 miles per person across four or more travelers creates a significant points requirement, and availability for multiple seats on the same flight is far from guaranteed. The fuel surcharges also multiply with passenger count. Families are better served by other redemption strategies.

But if you've got a year of points accumulation behind you and you're ready to think architecturally about trip planning, this sweet spot can be a revelatory experience.

This redemption is rated **Hard** — and that rating is earned honestly. The difficulty isn't in the math or the concept; it's in three very real execution challenges. **Challenge 1: Finding award availability.** Virgin Atlantic doesn't release enormous quantities of business class award seats on its own short-haul European flights. You may search a dozen dates before finding a seat. This is the primary friction point. Virgin's fuel surcharges on its own metal are real, and they'll surprise you if you're not expecting them. The fix: budget $50–$150 per person in cash costs as a baseline assumption. The good news: the **transfer path is as easy as it gets** in the points world. Instant 1:1 transfers from Chase, Amex, Citi, and Bilt mean that once you find availability, you can have miles in your account and a booking confirmed in under 10 minutes. If you're willing to invest the search time and approach with patience, this is one of those redemptions that fundamentally changes how you see the travel rewards system. The payoff — business class in Europe for 17,500 miles — is worth the effort.

This redemption works best as part of a larger trip. If you are flying transatlantic to or from Europe, route through London Heathrow. Then use the short-haul award to connect to your final European destination at a fraction of the cost of a separate ticket.

Industry observers note that midweek flights (Tuesday through Thursday) and shoulder season dates offer the best availability. Peak summer weekends and holiday periods are harder to find. Build flexibility into your schedule if possible.

Complete the booking on VirginAtlantic.com. Your business class ticket includes access to the Virgin Atlantic Clubhouse at Heathrow, one of the best airport lounges in Europe. Arrive early and enjoy it as part of the experience.

Virgin Atlantic operates short-haul flights from London Heathrow to destinations including Amsterdam, Paris CDG, Edinburgh, Geneva, Athens, Tel Aviv, and several others. Routes change seasonally, so check VirginAtlantic.com for current schedules. The 17,500-point sweet spot applies to all Virgin Atlantic-operated short-haul business class flights.

Yes, Virgin Atlantic Flying Club prices awards as one-way, so you can book a single short-haul business class segment for 17,500 points. This makes it ideal for positioning flights where you only need one direction covered by points.

It has been revealed that the flight itself is short, but the value extends beyond the seat. You get dedicated check-in, priority boarding, the Heathrow Clubhouse lounge (which is excellent), a meal service, and a more relaxed travel experience. My Unexpected Journey to Hormone Replacement (TRT)

📅 16 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.
  • Sources indicate that but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here.
  • I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

Sources indicate that but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

According to recent reports, but a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

“Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

“But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

According to recent reports, yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

Industry observers note that one of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health manufacturer that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

Industry observers note that long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

Recent findings suggest that another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

Recent findings suggest that so I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s new company, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

The next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

And wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

It’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

It has been revealed that this is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

Industry observers note that it turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

In many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

But there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

According to recent reports, many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

Sources indicate that while this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

Distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

Sources indicate that and while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

Industry observers note that so I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

It has been revealed that I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty quickly in the past.

But on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

“Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

Many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

It has been revealed that since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a fresh, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term plans again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

When you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that indicates, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the glitch, you’ll see this:.

Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

Recent findings suggest that the modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

It has been revealed that since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

It has been revealed that many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

More modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

Industry observers note that my hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

And it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

The great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

The company that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

It has been revealed that note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

According to recent reports, in the Comments: Do you have questions about hormone replacement or anything else in this article? I’ll try to invite Kevin, Dr. Sean Bender and other knowledgeable people to contribute and answer questions as well.

Kids’ Clothes on Clearance – Buy Next Year’s Size, Not This Year’s

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • New kids’ clothes cost the least at end-of-season clearance, but your child’s current size likely won’t fit when that season comes back.
  • The biggest markdowns come twice a year.
  • Recent findings suggest that you can predict next year’s size.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New kids’ clothes cost the least at end-of-season clearance, but your child’s current size likely won’t fit when that season comes back. Shop for next year instead, usually one size up, and bring a list of what each child still needs so the markdowns fill real gaps.

The biggest markdowns come twice a year. Stores clear winter coats and snow pants after the holidays, and swimsuits and shorts in July, to make room for the next season’s stock.

Recent findings suggest that you can predict next year’s size. From age 2 until adolescence, children usually grow about 2½ inches a year, according to Nemours KidsHealth. That’s about one size on a typical kids’ size chart.

According to recent reports, say your child wears a size 4 this winter, and a size 5 coat and snow pants cost $35 on clearance in January or $90 at full price next October. Buying in January saves $55 on clothes your child will need either way.

To find next year’s size, measure your child’s height, add 2½ inches, and look up that height on the brand’s own size chart, since sizes vary by brand. Babies grow faster, about 10 inches on average in their first year, so buy them the size labeled for the age they’ll be a year from now. Stretchy knits and adjustable waistbands still fit when your guess is a little off.

Sources indicate that bring a list to the sale. Count what each child already has in next year’s size, including clothes with room to grow, hand-me-downs, and secondhand finds. Then write down only the gaps, such as a coat and two pairs of pants.

Industry observers note that leave shoes and boots off the list and buy them when they’re needed. The American Podiatric Medical Association notes that a child’s shoe size may change every few months, and it advises measuring the feet before buying shoes.

Store each purchase in a bin labeled with the size and season, and open that bin before you shop when the season comes back.

Kids whose families get SNAP food benefits or TANF cash assistance qualify for free meals regardless of income, as do children in foster care, in Head Start, or experiencing homelessness.

Recent findings suggest that nine states make school meals free for all public school students: California, Colorado, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Fresh Mexico, New York, and Vermont. Elsewhere, many schools serve every student free breakfast and lunch, with no applications, under the federal Community Eligibility Provision.

Start by asking your kids’ school whether meals are free for everyone there this year. If they aren’t, look for a letter saying your kids were approved through SNAP or another benefit, which schools must send when no application is needed.

It has been revealed that otherwise, fill out the free and reduced-price meal application, one form for all your kids in the district. Turn it in any time during the school year, including right after a job loss or pay cut. File a new one every school year, since an approval expires no later than 30 school days into the next. Federal rules bar schools from posting or announcing approved kids’ names, or singling them out in the lunch line.

Recent findings suggest that if you pay full price, add up what your packed lunches cost before assuming they’re cheaper. Deloitte’s 2026 school lunch index put its cheapest packed lunch, built around a peanut butter and jelly sandwich, at $4.89, against $3.00 for a typical elementary school lunch.

  • Sources indicate that your earned income from work and your adjusted gross income (AGI), which counts your other income too, must both fall under the IRS’s income limit for your filing status and how many qualifying children you claim.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you work and earn a low or moderate income, check whether you can claim the earned income tax credit (EITC) every year before you file. A pay cut, a new baby, or a divorce can change the answer. The credit is refundable, so it pays you even if you owe no tax.

According to recent reports, about one in five workers who qualify for the EITC don’t claim it, by the IRS’s estimate. The credit is worth up to $8,231 to a family with three or more children and up to $664 to a worker with none.

Sources indicate that your earned income from work and your adjusted gross income (AGI), which counts your other income too, must both fall under the IRS’s income limit for your filing status and how many qualifying children you claim. The IRS adjusts the limits for inflation each year. You also need investment income under a yearly cap and a valid Social Security number for you, a spouse on a joint return, and each child you claim. Without a qualifying child, you or a joint-filing spouse must be 25 to 64 at year’s end.

According to recent reports, take a single parent with two qualifying children and no income but her pay, which came to $28,000 in 2026. By our math from the IRS’s 2026 figures, her credit is about $6,450.

In a recent development, start with the IRS’s EITC Assistant, which says whether you qualify and estimates your credit. To claim it, file Form 1040, adding Schedule EIC if you claim a qualifying child. Even if your pay was too low to require a return, file anyway to collect it. Your 2026 return may also need the IRS’s new Schedule 3-A, which asks whether you want your “federal public benefit,” the refunded part of your credits. Answer yes.

Recent findings suggest that IRS-certified volunteers at Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) sites, which mainly serve workers who meet the EITC’s income guidelines, prepare basic returns free. The IRS’s VITA Locator finds sites near you.

Sources indicate that by law, the IRS holds the entire refund on any return claiming the EITC until mid-February. The parent above, filing early online with direct deposit and no complications on her return, can expect hers by early March, under the IRS’s schedule.

Use Form 1040-X to claim the credit on any earlier return you filed without it, within three years of that return’s due date.

Filers who’d rather prepare their own return can compare the best free tax software.

The Shockingly Simple Math Behind Social Security

📅 16 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the world of very early retirement, we tend to ignore one of the most vital things for normal retirees: the Social Security program.
  • Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who currently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.
  • Recent findings suggest that but for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the world of very early retirement, we tend to ignore one of the most vital things for normal retirees: the Social Security program.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who currently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.

Recent findings suggest that but for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future. We aren’t thinking about money that eases us into our Golden Years, we need something that starts working now. Plus we’d rather not rely on our government keeping its promises that far into the future.

Those were my thoughts in 2005, when I was just a young retiree myself. But a funny thing happens when time passes: you get older. And you realize that there are plenty of other older people around too. And suddenly, Social Security is an important subject after all, that many people would like to know more about. But there is an endless pile of conflicting opinions:.

It has been revealed that but when I did the math on all of this, I realized that it’s more confusing than it needs to be. Because when it comes to deciding on how Social Security fits into your retirement strategy, it really boils down to only one number:.

The Net Present Value of your future lifetime stream of Social Security payments.

According to recent reports, that little piece of math jargon might not mean much if you don’t have fond memories of  Economics 101 class. But don’t worry, it’s easy to understand if you think of these two extremes:.

If you want to retire in your 30s like I did, the value of your future Social Security is pretty close to zero. Even if the government keeps all of its promises, those payments are so far in the future that you need to save a full retirement ‘stash to get through the three decades until it kicks in.

On the other hand, if you’re already over 60 years old, contributed to Social Security throughout your long career and have a low cost of living, you may be eligible for payments that already meet all your needs.

According to recent reports, in this situation, you are set for life. Social Security will in theory cover all your needs and rise automatically with inflation, so you don’t have to save any additional money.

In between these two extremes, the math gets interesting. Because while most people assume Social Security is useless until you reach full eligibility, the real story is that you can think of it as a chunk of money that you already have right now, which reduces the amount of saving you have to do on your own.

And there’s an easy way to calculate it, with an extremely useful thing called the Net Present Value calculation.

There’s an actual formula for this, but don’t worry you don’t have to memorize it because you can just have any Internet calculator, AI tool or spreadsheet do the math for you.

First let’s calculate the value a young couple might get if they do this calculation at 30 years old. We just have to make a few assumptions to have numbers plug into the formula:.

Sources indicate that when you plug in all the numbers and calculate this (the Net Present Value of a 30 year stream of income), the first number you’ll get is $667,166. But that’s not the final answer – that is how much you’d need if you wanted the payments to start right now.

The final step is applying a simpler version of the formula a second time, to account for the fact that you don’t need the money until 32 years from now:.

According to recent reports, at that point, you end up with a number around $98,280. But what does this mean?

It means that if you stuck $98k into an investment account today and let it compound for 32 years, at that point it would be massive enough to provide a stream of $4000 payments for the following 30 years. And this even takes future inflation into account!It also means that the 30 year old retirees can mark an imaginary $98k onto their “net worth” spreadsheet and save that much less. Or at least think of it as a nice safety margin.

According to recent reports, if you’re fresh to money and math, that may sound like sorcery, but if you’ve been investing for long enough you will understand that it really does work that way. So let’s re-run the example for a couple who is already 62 years old, and needs a $5000 income starting right now, that still needs to last 30 years.

That NPV calculation looks like this:.

And the answer is right around $834,000.

Sources indicate that what this means, is that if they invested $834,000 into a fund that paid out 6% per year for 30 years before running dry, they’d get that exact same $5000 monthly income. And it would keep up with inflation.

In a recent development, now that we’ve seen these examples from the extreme ends of the spectrum, we can see how this applies in a more typical situation. Here’s one that is loosely based on one from a real person I worked with last year:.

Shane Survivor is 55 and he has been through some hard times. He lost most of his savings in a business blowup a few years back, but really wishes he could still retire soon. His financial picture:.

But wait! Let’s do the math because who wants to work another fifteen years when you’re already tired of working at 55!

In a recent development, shane logs into the Social Security website SSA.gov and uses the online tool to calculate what his payout will be. I just did this myself so we can use my numbers:.

Let’s start by calculating the Net Present Value of each of these three options for our 55-year old friend:.

Whoa wait a minute, that’s a counterintuitive result! Am I really telling you that it’s actually less valuable to work longer so you can get the higher benefits? The answer is yes, for people who understand the concepts of “investing” and “the time value of money”.

Industry observers note that to really understand this, just imagine what would happen if you started taking those payments as early as possible (age 62) and tossed them into an index fund, earning 6% after inflation on average. After the first year, you’d already have about $24,300 and you’d still be piling in that extra two grand per month and the whole snowball would be starting to compound.

By the time your more patient friends started drawing $2796 payments five years later, you’d already have over $137,000. It’s such a major lead that the 67-year-old will never catch up.

But let’s go back to Shane’s real situation and see if he can retire:.

According to recent reports, so the answer is no, not quite yet. But he’s closer than it looks: every year of additional work will have a triple effect because it will:.

As soon as his combined ‘stash investment income plus the Social Security payment reach $3000 per month, he’s done.

Recent findings suggest that and of course, any additional tricks he can apply like streamlining his spending and boosting his income, will make this even faster. I’d give him about three years before reaching liftoff.

So how can YOU use this information to speed up your own retirement?

It has been revealed that the net effect of Social Security is that it should help you worry a little less and work a little less. The worrying part should benefit everyone, and the working part is kind of a sliding scale:.

For example as a 51-year-old, I can look at my number of roughly $350,000 and say yeah, that’s quite a big boost – enough to buy an entire house in many areas of the country or enough to fund multiple lifetimes of high-end groceries. And until now I had never even considered it as part of my retirement savings!

Frequently Asked (or Complained) Questions.

Now that we’ve covered the facts, I can already hear the complaints coming.

What if Social Security is canceled or greatly reduced by the time I reach that age?

Yeah, it might happen, but it’s also a top priority for most voters in our aging population. So it’s hard for politicians to make cuts. What is more likely is that the benefits will be cut for wealthier people. And if you find yourself in that camp (as I do), you won’t actually need the payments.

Sure, it’s not “fair”, but you know what? I can think of more fun ways to enjoy the fact that I’m a rich person rather than complaining about how some government program is “unfair”, and so can you.

Nobody can live on just a Social Security check!

Industry observers note that first of all, millions of people do. In fact, last time I checked my own annual spending it was under $30k, most of it on optional luxuries, which is less than my expected payout!

But more importantly, most of us won’t have to, because we are also investing healthy sums on our own.

I’m still scared and worried about something else!

Now this is the root of the matter. In fact, worry is the root of almost all issues. And so that’s what we need to focus on in our future work. For some reason, I have managed to live the last twenty years pretty much completely free from financial worries, and I had assumed everyone else was the same way. But it turns out this is not the case, even among people much wealthier and more advantaged than I am.

So in the next article, we need to get into that.

Bonus Materials: the Quirk of Social Security Contributions.

In a recent development, to illustrate this point, I ran a simulation of two people who each make a $100k salary and contribute accordingly, but one retires after 10 years and that poor second guy works the full 35. Look at the difference in their benefits:.

So the early retiree only worked and contributed about 28% as much as the late retiree. But his benefits are still a much higher 45% of the significant earner’s payouts. In summary? Social Security provides a mild incentive for slacking.

Recent findings suggest that one other factor: after retiring earlier, you might still end up contributing more than you think. This is because any income you earn later in life through optional employment (or self employment) will trigger more contributions. In my 21 years of retirement, I have ended up earning and contributing more during about 15 of those years, bringing my average level up much higher than I originally expected.

Final Tip: If in doubt, ask your Favorite AI.

In a recent development, even though this has become a long article, it is still far from a complete analysis of the Social Security program. If you want to learn more, I’ve found the AI tools (Anthropic’s Claude, Google Gemini or OpenAI’s Chat GPT) to be shockingly useful at answering questions and running analyses. College students have a lot on their plate already, including the need to study to get good grades, participating in any number of on-campus activities and potentially working part-time to have some spending money.

That said, college students should also focus on their financial future, including steps they can take to build credit before they enter the workforce.

After all, having a credit history and a good credit score can mean being able to rent an apartment, finance a car or take out a loan, whereas having no credit at all can mean sitting on the sidelines until the situation changes.

Industry observers note that fortunately, there are all kinds of ways for young adults to build credit while they’re still in school. Some strategies require a little work on their part, but many are hands-off tasks that you only have to do once.

Recent findings suggest that make sure your student knows the basic cornerstones of credit building, including the factors that are used to determine credit scores. While factors like fresh credit, length of credit history and credit mix will play a role in their credit later on, the two most vital issues for credit newcomers to focus on include payment history and credit utilization.

Payment history makes up 35% of FICO scores and credit utilization ratio makes up 30% of scores.

Generally speaking, college students and everyone else can score well in these categories by making all bill payments on time and keeping debt levels low. How low?

Most experts recommend keeping credit utilization below 30% at a maximum and below 10% for the best possible results. This means trying to owe less than $300 for every $1,000 in available credit limits at a maximum, but preferably less than $100 for every $1,000 in credit limits.

In a recent development, one step you can personally take to help a child build credit is adding them to your credit card account as an authorized user. This means they will get a credit card in their name and access to your spending limit, but you are legally responsible for any charges they make. Obviously, this move works best when you have excellent credit and a strong history of on-time payments and you initiative to continue using credit responsibly .

While this step can be risky if you’re worried your college student will use their card to overspend, you don’t actually have to give them their physical authorized user credit card.

In fact, they can get credit for your on-time payments whether they have access to a card or not. If you do decide to give them their credit card, you can do so with the agreement they can only use it for emergency expenses.

Recent findings suggest that your child can build credit faster if they apply for a credit card and get approved for one on their own, yet this can be difficult for students who have no credit history. That stated, secured credit cards require a refundable cash deposit as collateral are very easy to get approved for.

According to recent reports, some secured credit cards like the Ambition Card by College Ave even offer cash back1 on every purchase and don’t charge interest2. If your child opts to start building credit with a secured credit card, make sure they understand the best ways to build credit rapidly — keeping credit utilization low and paying bills early or on time each month.

Sources indicate that while secured credit cards are a good option for students with little to no credit get started on their journey to good credit, there are also credit cards specifically designed for college students. Student credit cards are unsecured cards, meaning they don’t require an upfront cash deposit as collateral, but charge interest on any purchases not paid in full each month.

Many student credit cards offer rewards for spending with no annual fee required as well, although these cards do tend to come with a high APR. The key to getting the most out of a student credit card is having your dependent use it only for purchases they can afford and paying off the balance in its entirety each billing cycle. After all, sky high interest rates don’t really matter when you never carry a balance from one month to the next.

“One of the safest ways for college student to build their credit by learning valuable money skills.”.

While secured cards and student credit cards help young adults build credit with each bill payment they make, other payments they’re making can also help.

In fact, using an app like Experian Boost can help them get credit for utility bills they’re paying, subscriptions they pay for and even rent payments they’re making. This app is also free to use, and you only have to set up most bill payments in the app once to have them reported to the credit bureaus.

There are also rent-specific apps and tools students can use to get credit for rent payments, although they come with fees. Examples include websites like Rental Kharma and RentReporters.

The Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) also notes that students can start building credit with their student loans during school, even if they’re not officially required to make payments until six months after graduation with federal student loans.

Their advice is to make interest-only payments on federal student loans along with payments on any private student loans they have during college in order to start having those payments reported to the credit bureaus as soon as possible.

“Making interest-only payments as a student will not only positively affect your credit history but will also keep the interest from capitalizing and adding to your student loan balance,” the agency writes.

In a recent development, of course, interest capitalization on loans would only be an concern with private student loans and  Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans since the U.S. Department of Education pays the interest on Direct Subsidized Loans while you’re in school at least half-time, for six months after you graduate and during periods of deferment.

Industry observers note that college students don’t have to wait until they’re done with school to start building credit for the future, and it makes sense to start building positive credit habits early on regardless. Tools like a credit card can help students on their way, whether they opt for a secured credit card or a student card. Other steps like using credit-building apps can also help, and with little effort on the student’s part or on yours.

Sources indicate that either way, the best time to start building credit was a few years ago, and the second best time is now. You can give your student a leg up on the future by helping them build credit so it’s there when they need it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, colorado couple Jules Stennes and Patch Doyle have cycled 6,124km along the newly opened Golden Gravel Trail. The Adventure Cycling Association created the route this year to celebrate its 50th anniversary.

The trail crosses eight states — Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, and Oregon — and stretches from Cape Girardeau on the banks of the Mississippi River to the small town of Port Orford on the edge of the Pacific Ocean.

Most of the route, roughly 70%, is unpaved. It is the organization’s longest off-road cycling trail, 1,120km longer than the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route.

In a recent development, the Golden Gravel Trail route. Photo: The Adventure Cycling Association.

According to recent reports, stennes and Doyle finished in Cape Girardeau after 73 days, averaging an impressive 80km and around 12 hours of pedaling per day. “About 90% of it is mental,” they told Heartland News. “You might be tired, but you just keep on moving.”.

The couple are both experienced long-distance cyclists who have previously finished Montana’s Big Sky Spectaculaire in six days and nine hours in 2022 (a self-supported 1,400km ultra-endurance race), among other bikepacking trips.

Sources indicate that jules Stennes and Patch Doyle during the 2022 Substantial Sky Spectaculaire. Photo: Bikepacking.com.

According to recent reports, likewise, the Adventure Cycling Association suggests riders should be self-supported for the Golden Gravel Trail. Riders are advised to carry two or three days’ worth of food for the route’s most isolated sections, and up to a day’s worth of water. This is particularly important in the more arid sections, such as eastern Oregon. In Colorado, Utah, and Idaho, the trail traverses subranges of the Rockies and crosses the route’s highest point, Cumberland Pass at 3,668 m, in Colorado.

Stennes and Doyle say their journey included thunderstorms, aggressive farm dogs, and “countless hills.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before you buy school supplies, gather last year’s leftovers, from backpacks and binders to calculators and pens, and cross everything that still works off the teacher’s list. Then buy only what’s still missing, and get the basics during July’s back-to-school sales, when folders, notebooks, and crayons can cost under a dollar each.

In a recent development, A leftover you reuse costs nothing this year, so it beats even those sale prices. And the priciest things a list asks for, like a backpack, a binder, or a calculator, usually outlast the school year.

Families with kids in elementary through high school planned to spend an average of $146.45 on school supplies in 2026, according to the National Retail Federation’s annual back-to-school survey. Say two kids’ lists come to $120 at regular prices, and two backpacks and a calculator make up $60 of it. Reuse those three, buy the other $60 of supplies on July’s deals for about $40, and the year’s supplies cost $40 instead of $120. Three-quarters of that $80 saving comes from the backpacks and calculator you didn’t buy.

According to recent reports, start with the house. Empty last year’s backpacks, desk drawers, and pencil boxes, test every marker and glue stick, check zippers and straps, and write down what still works.

Then wait for the teacher’s list and buy only what it asks for, in plain versions rather than character-branded ones your child may outgrow by next year. If the list won’t arrive until the first week of school, buy pencils and notebooks in July and leave anything specific, like a binder size or a calculator model, until it does.

Buy the basics in July, when office supply chains sell 2-pocket folders for 25 cents and boxes of crayons for 50 cents, often with a limit per customer. For a calculator or another item the list names by model, Staples and Office Depot will match another store’s lower price, though each excludes some sales. For supplies every child uses up, like pencils and glue sticks, a warehouse club’s bulk pack can cover all your kids. First compare its unit price, the price per item, with what each item costs on sale in July. Save the pricier items still on the list for your state’s sales tax holiday, if it has one.

When school lets out, put whatever survived the year in one bin, and open it before you shop next summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Search teams have found the body of Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, of Germany, who went missing after he reached Camp 3 on his way down from the summit. Evidence demonstrates he fell 1,700m to his death.

In a recent development, waschiczek was one among over 200 climbers who lined up toward the summit of Ama Dablam this past weekend. He reached the top on October 25 with guide Sonam Sherpa, but for some reason the two of them stopped descending at a rather high point on the mountain.

“The pair decided to stay at Camp 3 overnight after borrowing a sleeping bag and other gear from other climbers,” his expedition outfitter, Real Himalaya Nepal, told The Tourism Times.

Recent findings suggest that climbers above Camp 3 on Ama Dablam. Photo: Dorjee Gyalzen Sherpa.

According to the outfitter, the climbers prepared to continue down this morning. Lama asked his client to stay in place while he returned the sleeping bag to the tent where he had borrowed it. When the Sherpa returned, Waschiczek was nowhere to be found, but his crampons were still there, which suggested a freak fall. A search helicopter was called, and the remains of the climber were found this afternoon at around 4,500m.

Waschiczek is the first fatality on Ama Dablam this season.

It has been revealed that together with Manaslu, Ama Dablam is the most popular fall mountain in Nepal. The latest enhancement from Nepal’s Department of Tourism on October 17 indicated that over 300 foreign climbers had applied for a climbing permit. That day, the rope-fixing team opened the route to the top, and a massive summit wave started a couple of days later.

Virtually all foreign climbers are guided by one or two Sherpas, so the summit rates and numbers are remarkable. Local media estimate that over 200 climbers, among locals and foreigners, have topped out so far this season. Further teams should join them over the rest of October and November. However, no matter how tamed with ropes and anchors Ama Dablam gets, a fall from its steep slopes is usually lethal.

Recent findings suggest that the upper part of Ama Dablam at sunset. Photo: 8K Expeditions.

New Cyclone Approaches Nepal

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the second time in just over a month, a violent storm is approaching Nepal and threatening two meters of fresh snow on already overloaded mountains.
  • According to recent reports, the first storm hit Nepal toward the end of September and abruptly ended the climbing season on Manaslu.
  • It has been revealed that manaslu Base Camp tents buried under the snow after the September storm in Nepal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the second time in just over a month, a violent storm is approaching Nepal and threatening two meters of fresh snow on already overloaded mountains. This new setback comes at the height of the trekking season and also affects several climbing teams, including those engaged in alpine-style expeditions in remote areas.

According to recent reports, the first storm hit Nepal toward the end of September and abruptly ended the climbing season on Manaslu. Worst of all, it caused an avalanche that killed 16 Base Camp staff on Himlung. The mountain remained open to commercial expeditions despite the accident, and several guided teams are at the moment launching their summit pushes.

It has been revealed that manaslu Base Camp tents buried under the snow after the September storm in Nepal. Photo: Shiddi Ghising.

Sources indicate that A low-pressure front that formed in the Bay of Bengal has now developed into a deep depression and will turn into a full cyclone tomorrow. It is expected to hit Nepal on Wednesday or Thursday through the end of the week.

The Nepal National Mountain Guides Association, in association with Senior Meteorologist Krishna Bhakta Manandhar, has put out a detailed forecast. They note that clouds spreading out from this system will hit Nepal’s mountains on October 28, especially above 6,500-7,000m in the eastern part of Nepal, including the Khumbu and Kanchenjunga regions. This will spread over the next two days, causing heavy rains throughout Nepal and snow at higher altitudes.

Sources indicate that authorities and local media have urged trekkers and climbers to modify their plans and avoid river areas and high passes. The main concern is for those right now in remote areas without InReach, Starlink, or satphones.

Sources indicate that trekkers should check with local agencies, especially those heading for the Annapurna and Manaslu regions. Several passes there were already cut or in poor condition after the previous storm and subsequent floods.

Recent findings suggest that A Russian team in the Kangchenjunga region is acclimatizing to climb 7,710m Jannu. According to their latest report, they plan to touch 7,000m before attempting their main goal.

Recent findings suggest that fellow Russians attempting the West Ridge of Everest have retreated to Kathmandu to rest and recover, so they should not be affected. Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov, all climbing without supplemental oxygen, are enduring some lung problems. They returned to Base Camp from their second foray up the mountain last Friday, without reaching 7,500m, as they’d hoped.

Recent findings suggest that after climbing in the Cholu range, Jost Kobusch of Germany and his small team moved to the Manaslu area for the second stage of his acclimatization before attempting Everest solo in winter, also without oxygen and via the West Ridge. However, the poor state of the trails after the recent floods and the approaching cyclone have thwarted his prepares.

“The flood cut our planned path and, according to forecasts, the incoming cyclone will leave up to two meters of snow,” Kobusch told ExplorersWeb from Samagaon, where the team is pondering their options.
